Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14223512/assets/310d05d05284201c4914de171e6ee6a7574784da4c9bf7d4e442cdf2a210722d.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slope lines on the same vertical line are all the same. This means that the slope does not vary with $y.$ In other words, ${y}^{′}$ is a function of $x$ only.

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\  & {y}^{′}={e}^{x} \\  & {y}^{′}={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the slopes become vertical as $x\to 0.$ 

Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Notice that

$$
|{y}^{′}|=|\frac{1}{x}|\to \infty \,\text{as}\,x\to 0.
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x}$ become vertical as $x\to 0.$
By contrast, 

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{x}\to 1\,\text{as}\,x\to 0,
$$

and

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}\to 0\,\text{as}\,x\to 0.
$$

Therefore, the required equation is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$
